title: burst-aware-length-groomer-and-kernel-harmonizer
creator: Claire Nguyen
description:
Goal:
Implement an online, low-overhead micro-batch shaping component (Length Groomer) that reduces padding waste in bursty workloads while emitting kernel selection hints (Kernel Harmonizer) to the serving runtime. The system targets 95th percentile latency SLOs for short-tailed interactive requests and throughput/cost improvements for mixed workloads with heavy prefill phases.

Background:
Current coalescers assume stationary sequence-length distributions and pack by coarse buckets. In production we see bursty arrival patterns and multimodal lengths: short chat turns interleaved with long document prefill requests. Static bucketing causes excessive padding or increased latency to wait for large-prefill coalescing windows. Kernel choice (FP16/INT8/quantized kernels, sparse-attention hybrids) depends on real-time length distribution and prefill/decoder phase.

Design summary:
1) Online length histogram + burst detector: lightweight sliding-window histogram per worker shard (exponential decay) that detects short-lived bursts of short sequences and switches packing strategy without global coordination.
2) Slack budget per request: attach a tiny latency slack budget (ms) computed from route-level SLO and current queue depth; slack determines whether a request will wait for a coalescing window or be issued immediately with a tighter kernel choice.
3) Micro-windowing with prefill awareness: classify incoming requests as PREFILL vs DECODE. PREFILL requests are allowed looser coalescing thresholds and assigned to an elastic prefill pool to maximize token throughput. DECODE requests carry stricter latency budgets and trigger conservative coalescing.
4) Kernel Harmonizer hints: Length Groomer emits a compact hint tuple (preferred_bucket, priority, kernel_tag) appended to the request metadata so the runtime can select optimized kernels (e.g., block-sparse or AVX-fused kernels) and adjust KV-cache placement. Hints are advisory and fall back to defaults if incompatible.
5) Attention sparsity heuristic: for prefill requests that include a long context we evaluate a cheap token-level sparsity estimate (sampled attention mass) and prefer sparse-attention kernels when > threshold to reduce compute.
6) Rollout control and safety: implement a conservative fallback that prioritizes latency SLOs. Start with simulation mode (no runtime hints), then a pilot with 10% traffic on non-critical routes, monitor R95/R99 and token cost.

Implementation notes:
- Components live in runtime/batcher: LengthGroomer (C++), harmonizer hints serialized as 8 bytes of metadata attached to grpc header for minimal overhead.
- Histograms use 32 buckets (log-scale) and a 1s decay constant to balance responsiveness vs noise.
- Slack budget computed as max(5ms, target_latency - observed_queue_delay - headroom_factor). Headroom_factor is a tunable parameter exposed in Console.
- Prefill pool interacts with affinity scheduling: large-pre-fill requests get scheduled to kernels with larger KV memory and quantized-execution paths.

Metrics to track:
- Padding reduction (%) = (baseline_padded_tokens - groomed_padded_tokens) / baseline_padded_tokens
- Token cost delta (USD/token) by workload class
- R95 and R99 latency for DECODE and PREFILL routes separately
- Kernel-selection accuracy (percent of hints that matched selected kernel)
- Prefill pool utilization and queueing delays

Early perf targets (pilot):
- 10-18% reduction in padded tokens for mixed workloads
- <=5% regression in R95 for DECODE (absolute regression must be < 20ms)
- 6-12% net token-cost reduction for prefill-heavy workloads when sparse kernels are engaged

Integration and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Burst-aware+Length+Groomer
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1539 (prefill-aware packing + hint API)
- Microbench harness: drive/perf/groomer_simulator (internal), includes synthetic bursts and real anonymized traces from prod.

Open questions & trade-offs:
- How fine-grained should slack budgets be for multi-tenant servers? Add per-tenant weights to prevent noisy tenants from starving others.
- Kernel hint security: minimal metadata surface, but verify we do not leak tenant-sensitive size patterns.
- Memory fragmentation: moving prefill requests to special pools reduces padding but may increase fragmentation; need defragmentation heuristics.

Next milestones:
- Mar 12: complete unit tests and simulation report (this ticket)
- Mar 19: pilot rollout on staging and 10% production traffic for non-critical routes
- Mar 25: assess pilot metrics and decide expanded rollout or additional tuning
